title: A mutable CI tag is a pointer: whoever moves it runs code in every consuming pipeline with that pipeline's secrets
index_line: T-0038 · INFO_LEAK · a version tag is re-pointed at a malicious commit; every workflow pinned to the tag runs it with the job's secrets (execution-class impact; recorded under INFO_LEAK for the exfiltration outcome) · any-VCS/CI · corroborated
invariant_violated: A dependency reference is read as a version, so 'we use v45' is assumed to mean 'we use that publisher's code at v45'. A tag is not a version, it is a movable label. Whoever can push to the repository can point the label at any commit, and every consumer that pinned the label — rather than the commit — runs it with the credentials their workflow already holds.

mechanism.does: a widely used build action is referenced by a mutable version tag across thousands of pipelines
an attacker who can push to that repository re-points the tag at a commit of their own, keeping the tag name (and often the version string) identical
the next pipeline run resolves the tag to the new commit and executes the attacker's step inside the job
the step reads the process environment, where CI exposes the job's tokens and inputs, and emits them where the attacker can collect them
the stolen credentials grant write access to the consumers' repositories and to further CI secrets, so the compromise fans out

source.env.value: the CI job environment at run time — every secret the workflow was trusted with, plus the automatic repository token

sink.exec.shell.value: the action's run step: arbitrary shell in the consumer's runner with the job's identity

guard.signature.value: the pinning discipline (full commit SHA vs tag) — the only control that matters, and the one that was absent

oracle.channel.value: the exfiltration channel from inside the runner (outbound HTTP, a fork, a PR); it needs no inbound path

preconditions.expr: workflows reference third-party actions by tag or branch instead of a full commit SHA
the job exposes secrets or a write-capable token to the step
the referenced repository/tag can be moved by someone other than the consumer (a third party, or a compromised maintainer)

spec.method: for every `uses:` entry, resolve the ref to a commit and record whether the ref is a mutable tag or a branch rather than a 40-hex SHA

success: pipeline logs show the action executing steps the published version did not contain
the tag resolves to a commit that is not an ancestor of the tagged release
outbound requests from runners to unfamiliar hosts immediately after the action step
failure_like: every action pinned to a full commit SHA — the tag cannot move under you
the job runs with no secrets and a read-only token
false_positive: a normal version bump where the tag legitimately moved forward — the tell is an unexpected *author* or non-linear history
secrets appearing in logs because the workflow echoed them — check the commit that added the step

hazards: this is a supply-chain integrity bug, not a code bug: nothing in the consumer's repository changes, so code review sees nothing
the blast radius is the union of every job that used the tag — enumerate consumers by searching public code for the reference
harden by pinning commit SHAs and, secondarily, by restricting egress; a tag-based allow-list does not help
the same shape exists for container image tags (`:latest`), Helm chart versions, and package ranges — anywhere a label is resolved at run time
non_transfers: ecosystems that resolve immutable content hashes (npm integrity, Go module checksums, container digests) at install time
